intro: How a film or a play is made, who does what, and how to give your opinion of what you have seen.

palabras.consejo: It has no accent: it is a single syllable. The person who writes it is the «guionista».
The o becomes ue: «ruedo», «ruedas», «rueda». The past «rodó» does not change.
It comes from «rodar». A shoot can last weeks or months, with many people working.
The verb is «estrenar»: «la película se estrena el viernes». You also «estrenas» a new suit.
It is feminine: «la banda sonora». It includes the music and the songs of the film.
It comes from «decorar». On screen it looks real, but it may be made of cardboard or wood.
In a gym, «el vestuario» is where you change clothes. Here it is the clothing of the show.
You say «hacer el papel de» or «interpretar un papel». It is also the paper you write on.
An actor interprets a role and a musician, a song. The noun is «la interpretación».
It is also handing out things: «el reparto de pizzas». It comes from «repartir».
The ll sounds like y: ta-KI-ya. An «éxito de taquilla» sells lots of tickets.
In the cinema each «butaca» has a number. It is also a comfortable armchair at home.
In Spain almost every foreign film is dubbed. It also means to fold: «doblar una carta».
On cinema listings it is written «VO»: «en versión original con subtítulos».
From «parecer», to seem. «Me ha parecido» means it seemed to me.
In the theatre and cinema, an actor «interpreta» a role.
Feminine of «magnífico». The tilde marks the stress on NI.
From «decorar». In a film, the «decorados» are built on purpose.
Plural of «impresionante». The ci sounds like «sy» in Spain.
«Durar» is to last. The stress is on RO.
In Spain, «doblar» a film means to dub it into Spanish.
The -ía ending is the conditional: «yo ganaría».
The g before e sounds like «h»: e-le-hi-RE-mos.
With «habrá», it is the past participle: «habrá durado».
The c before o sounds like «k»: FO-kos. «El foco» is masculine.
«Convertir» changes e to «ie» in the stress: convierto, convierten.
The accent on the first syllable shows the stress: TEK-ni-kos.
Agrees with «madera», feminine: «pintada».
The g before e sounds like «h»: KHES-to.
«Actor» is used for men and women: «la actriz» is the feminine form.
«Echar a andar» means to start walking.
The stress is at the end: an-DAR. Also means «to work» as a machine.
Its family is «letra», letter. A sign is a piece of letters.
The c before i sounds like «th». Masculine: «el terciopelo».
The j sounds like a strong «h»: KRU-jen.
The opposite of «encender», to turn on.
Feminine of «lento», agreeing with «música».
The au is one diphthong: a-PLAU-de.
«De pie» means standing up. The word is short: PYE.
«Estrenar» is to use or show something for the first time.
«Rodar» means to film a movie. Stress on DO.
«Actuar» can mean to act on stage or simply to behave.
From «suponer», to suppose. The -ción ending is always feminine.

texto:
**Making a film.** The scriptwriter writes the **guion** (script). The director picks the **reparto** (cast) and **rueda** (shoots) the film: the **rodaje** (shoot) lasts weeks or months. You need **decorados** (sets), **vestuario** (costumes), special effects and a **banda sonora** (soundtrack).

**Acting.** An actor **interpreta** (plays) a **papel** (role). The protagonist is the main character.

**Watching it.** The film **se estrena** (opens): the **estreno** is the premiere. Tickets are bought at the **taquilla** (box office) and each viewer sits in a **butaca** (seat). In Spain almost all films are **dobladas** (dubbed), but there is also **versión original** with subtitles.

**Giving an opinion.** «La película trata de…», «El guion es previsible», «Vale la pena verla». An «éxito de taquilla» is a film that sells many tickets.

**Note.** The word **guion** is written without an accent.

Besides talking about tomorrow, the future is used to **guess**:

- **About the present:** **Serán las diez** (I think it is ten o'clock).
- **About the past**, with **habrá** + participle: **El rodaje habrá durado meses** (I suppose the shoot lasted months).
- **To concede a point:** **No será una obra maestra, pero…** (I admit that perhaps it is not, but…).

In spoken language it is used a lot to give an opinion cautiously.

ejemplos.estudio: El rodaje habrá durado muchos meses.
ejemplos.alumno: The shoot must have lasted many months.
It may not be a masterpiece.
It must be ten o'clock now.

frases.alumno: What did you think of the film?

frases.estudio: La protagonista interpreta su papel de forma magnífica.
frases.alumno: The lead actress plays her role magnificently.
analisis: interpreta su papel de forma magnífica

frases.estudio: El guion me ha parecido demasiado previsible.
frases.alumno: I found the script too predictable.

frases.estudio: La banda sonora y los decorados son impresionantes.
frases.alumno: The soundtrack and the sets are stunning.
analisis: La banda sonora y los decorados

frases.estudio: Dicen que el rodaje duró dos años.
frases.alumno: They say the shoot lasted two years.
analisis: Dicen que el rodaje duró dos años
que el rodaje duró dos años

frases.estudio: No entiendo que la hayan doblado.
frases.alumno: I do not understand why they have dubbed it.
analisis: No entiendo que la hayan doblado

frases.alumno: In the original version it would gain a lot.

frases.estudio: Aunque no será una obra maestra, ha sido un éxito de taquilla.
frases.alumno: Although it may not be a masterpiece, it has been a box-office hit.
analisis: Aunque no será una obra maestra ha sido un éxito de taquilla
Aunque no será una obra maestra

frases.estudio: La próxima vez elegiremos butacas en la última fila.
frases.alumno: Next time we will choose seats in the back row.
analisis: La próxima vez elegiremos butacas en la última fila

frases.estudio: En la plaza del pueblo, los focos convierten la noche en un día de cartón.
frases.alumno: In the village square, the spotlights turn the night into a cardboard day.
analisis: convierten la noche en un día de cartón

frases.estudio: Los técnicos mueven con cuidado los decorados de madera pintada.
frases.alumno: The technicians carefully move the sets made of painted wood.
analisis: mueven con cuidado los decorados de madera pintada

frases.estudio: El vestuario huele a polvo y a lluvia reciente.
frases.alumno: The costumes smell of dust and recent rain.
analisis: huele a polvo y a lluvia reciente
a polvo y a lluvia reciente

frases.estudio: La directora levanta una mano y pide silencio con un gesto.
frases.alumno: The director raises a hand and asks for silence with a gesture.
analisis: levanta una mano y pide silencio con un gesto

frases.estudio: Al oír la palabra «acción», los actores echan a andar entre los focos como sombras.
frases.alumno: On hearing the word «action», the actors set off among the spotlights like shadows.
analisis: echan a andar entre los focos como sombras

frases.estudio: Meses después, el estreno llena la sala del viejo cine de la avenida.
frases.alumno: Months later, the premiere fills the hall of the old cinema on the avenue.
analisis: llena la sala del viejo cine de la avenida
la sala del viejo cine de la avenida
del viejo cine de la avenida

frases.estudio: En la taquilla, una cola larga espera bajo las luces rojas del letrero.
frases.alumno: At the box office, a long queue waits under the red lights of the sign.
analisis: espera bajo las luces rojas del letrero
bajo las luces rojas del letrero

frases.estudio: Dentro, las butacas de terciopelo crujen cuando el público se sienta.
frases.alumno: Inside, the velvet seats creak when the audience sits down.
analisis: crujen cuando el público se sienta

frases.estudio: Cuando se apagan las luces, la banda sonora llena la sala de una música lenta.
frases.alumno: When the lights go out, the soundtrack fills the hall with slow music.
analisis: llena la sala de una música lenta

frases.estudio: Al final, el público aplaude de pie durante varios minutos.
frases.alumno: At the end, the audience applauds standing for several minutes.
analisis: aplaude de pie durante varios minutos

pregunta.texto: What is the music of a film called?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: the soundtrack is the music and songs of the film.
The cast is the group of actors, not the music.
The costumes are the actors' clothes.

pregunta.texto: Which verb means opening in cinemas for the first time?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «estrenarse» is opening in cinemas for the first time.
«Rodar» is shooting the film; it is not showing it.
«Doblar» is adding voices in another language.

frase.texto: La película se rodó en solo seis semanas

piezas.traduccion: The film was shot in just six weeks

pregunta.texto: What does an actor who plays a role do?

opciones.explicacion: Writing the script is the scriptwriter's job.
Yes: playing a role is acting as a character.
Tickets are sold at the box office.

pregunta.texto: Write in Spanish: «the seat» (in the cinema).
Where do you buy the tickets?

frase.texto: Las entradas se compran en la ____.

piezas.traduccion: Las entradas se compran en la ____.

opciones.explicacion: The «butaca» is the seat you sit in, not where you pay.
The soundtrack is the film's music.
Yes: the «taquilla» is the window where tickets are bought.

pregunta.texto: What does the future express in «Serán las diez»?

opciones.explicacion: It does not speak of tomorrow: it speaks of the time it is now.
It orders nothing: it only guesses a time.
Yes: it is a way of saying «creo que son las diez».
